findings.source_quote: τοὺς λειποτάκτας ἐπιστρεφέτωσαν, τοῦ μὴ ἐπιλείπειν τοὺς συνερχομένους τῶν λόγων ἐπακούειν
findings.english_quote: They should bring back those who desert their posts, so as not to abandon those who come together to listen to the discourses
findings.issue: The draft’s transitive construction is conceivable and its uncertainty is disclosed, but it gives priority to a less contextually supported reading. Taking τοὺς συνερχομένους as the infinitive’s accusative subject and ἐπακούειν as complementary to ἐπιλείπειν connects restoring deserters directly with continued attendance and hearing. The main rendering instead makes the purpose the deacons’ avoidance of abandoning the assembled people.
findings.suggested_revision: Prefer provisionally: “They should bring back those who desert their posts, so that those who assemble do not cease listening to the discourses.” Retain the transitive “not abandon those who assemble” construction as an explicitly unresolved alternative. This proposed replacement requires fresh review; the supplied Greek does not require correction or renewed print verification.

findings.source_quote: καὶ τῷ ἀγνοοῦντι πλήθει προσαντιβαλλέτωσαν, ἵν’ ἐπιφαίνωνται
findings.english_quote: and bring them to the attention of the multitude that is unaware, so that they may appear
findings.issue: The notes correctly disclose uncertainty, but “appear” remains an insufficiently explained lexical gloss. In this care-of-the-sick context, appearing or coming on the scene may concern attendance or visitation, rather than simply becoming visible. Neither that contextual force nor the subject of ἐπιφαίνωνται is settled. This is an unresolved meaning problem, not evidence of source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Compare attested uses of προσαντιβάλλω and ἐπιφαίνομαι, especially constructions involving notification and attendance. Evaluate “so that they may come forward” or, if the visitation sense is established, “so that they may come to visit them.” Explicitly identify the inferred subject and disclose that “visit them” supplies a contextual interpretation rather than separately expressed Greek words. Preserve the existing alternatives until that semantic review is completed.
